name: generator-comparison-v1
question: Does the research PROCESS improve: fewer false premises, more executable and informative candidates, fewer duplicates, at what cost? (process efficiency; NOT evidence of financial edge)

C.memory: lessons from archived tasks of arm_guided, arm_random, claude_session, claude_cli and its own lab

common.mode: research (no auto-activation, so every task compares to v0)
common.premise_stage: applied to all arms (offline operators carry fixed premises)
common.evaluation: unchanged evaluator, frozen promotion rule research-protocol-v2, same data
common.validation_trials: each pilot lab inherits all earlier validation trials (DSR N)

metrics.premise_correct_rate: tasks whose premise check is 'accepted' / tasks that produced a hypothesis
metrics.executable_rate: tasks reaching EVALUATE (passed static, sandbox, determinism, causality) / tasks that produced a candidate
metrics.duplicate_rate: tasks whose candidate code hash already exists in any lab, or flagged duplicate / tasks with a candidate
metrics.informative_task: a task that reached EVALUATE (a development measurement of the candidate exists)
metrics.cost_per_informative: wall-clock s, sandbox runs, LLM calls/tokens and API-equivalent USD per informative task (API-equivalent USD is the CLI's total_cost_usd field: an ESTIMATE, not observed billing)
metrics.mechanism_observed_rate: informative tasks whose declared mechanism metric moved as predicted on development
metrics.robustness: share of informative tasks classified unstable_across_periods (lower is better)
metrics.confirmed: promotions under the frozen rule (exploratory: the validation split is reused and not independent)

pilot.purpose: check mechanisms and measure cost; no inferential claim

full_study_plan.justification: the primary process metric is a proportion (premise_correct_rate); with 30 tasks per arm a difference of ~0.35 between 0.5 and 0.85 is detectable at alpha 0.05 with ~80% power (two-proportion test); smaller differences need more runs
full_study_plan.analysis: per-arm proportions with Wilson intervals; arm differences by Fisher exact test with Holm correction over the metric family; campaign-level bootstrap for costs
full_study_plan.budget_gate: requires explicit user approval of the estimated plan quota measured in the pilot
